sources.title: Food Network — Ree Drummond’s Beef with Snow Peas

exactBodyChange.before:
## Chef's Note

Thinly cut flank steak and brief cooking keep this stir-fry tender. Divide the sauce before it touches raw beef and use a clean plate for cooked meat. Cook in batches so the steak sears instead of steaming.

## Directions

1. **Mix:** In a bowl, mix together the soy sauce, sherry, cornstarch, brown sugar and ginger. Add the beef to a separate bowl and pour one-third of the liquid over the top. Save the rest of the liquid. Toss the beef and set aside.

2. **Cook:** Heat the oil in a heavy skillet (iron is best) over high heat. Add the snow peas and stir for 45 seconds, getting as much color on them as possible. Remove to a plate.

3. **Finish:** Allow the skillet to get very hot again. With tongs, add half the meat mixture, leaving most of the marinade still in the bowl. Spread out the meat as you add it to skillet, but do not stir for a good minute. (You want the meat to get as brown as possible as quickly as possible.) Sprinkle half the scallions over the meat. Flip the meat to the other side and cook for another 30 seconds. Remove to a clean plate.

4. **Continue:** Repeat with the other half of the meat, allowing the skillet to get very hot again first. After flipping, add the first plateful of meat, the reserved liquid, the crushed red pepper and snow peas. Stir over high heat for 30 seconds, and then turn off the heat. Check the seasonings and add salt only if it needs it. The mixture will thicken as it sits. Use a clean plate for the first cooked batch. Discard the raw-contact marinade; the reserved sauce must have been kept separate. Check beef for 145°F / 63°C and allow three minutes before serving. Serve immediately over rice.
exactBodyChange.after:
## Chef's Note

Slice flank steak thinly across the grain and divide the sauce before it touches raw meat. Cook the beef in uncrowded batches and keep the cooked batch on a clean plate. Add the second half of the scallions with the second beef batch so all the listed scallions reach the finished dish.

## Directions

1. **Divide the sauce:** Whisk soy sauce, sherry, cornstarch, brown sugar and ginger until smooth. Pour one-third into a separate bowl with the thinly sliced beef; keep the other two-thirds clean for finishing. Toss beef to coat and keep refrigerated while preparing the pan.
2. **Cook snow peas:** Heat the full listed oil in a heavy skillet or wok over medium-high heat until shimmering, without letting it smoke. Add trimmed snow peas and stir until bright and crisp-tender, starting checks after about 45 seconds. Transfer to a plate.
3. **Cook beef batches and all scallions:** Bring the pan back to cooking heat. Lift half the beef from its coating with tongs, leaving excess marinade in the raw bowl, and spread in a thin layer. Add half the sliced scallions. Let the first side brown, starting checks around 1 minute, then turn and continue as needed. Transfer to a clean plate. Repeat with the other half of BOTH beef and scallions. If the pan needs more than two loads, divide both ingredients across those loads rather than crowding it. Discard the unused raw-contact marinade; do not use that bowl for cooked food.
4. **Finish and check:** Return cooked beef and snow peas to the pan. Restir the clean reserved sauce and add it with crushed red pepper. Stir over heat until the sauce gently bubbles and thickens and all the beef reaches 145°F /63°C. Remove from heat and rest at least 3 minutes before serving. Taste with a clean spoon and add the listed salt allowance only as needed.
5. **Serve:** Serve over jasmine or long-grain rice cooked separately according to its package instructions.
